package_info.why_malicious: This article is an educational overview of software supply chain security and does not analyze or describe any specific malicious package. It discusses attack vectors, real-world incidents, and best practices, but does not provide code or package-level details for any particular malware.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected execution of arbitrary commands during package installation (e.g., npm postinstall scripts)
Network requests to unknown or suspicious domains during install or runtime
Access to sensitive files (e.g., SSH keys, config files) by third-party packages
Typosquatting or dependency confusion: installation of packages with names similar to legitimate ones
file_indicators: Presence of install scripts in package.json (npm) or setup.py (PyPI) that execute shell commands
Unusual or unexpected files in package distributions (e.g., binaries, obfuscated scripts)
Sensitive information (API keys, credentials) stored in code or configuration files
network_indicators: Outbound connections to domains not associated with the legitimate package or vendor
Use of public file-sharing or webhook services for data exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor package installation and build processes for unexpected command execution, network activity, or file access. Use automated tools to scan dependencies for known malicious packages and typosquatting attempts. Review package manifests for install scripts or binaries. Audit code and configuration for accidental exposure of secrets. Employ behavioral monitoring to detect suspicious activity during install or runtime.
